stops.note: 'day of the Moon'; the seven-day planetary week spread through the Roman world in the 1st century AD, and a graffito at Pompeii lists the days by their planetary gods
Germanic peoples translated the Latin planetary day names into their own tongue, mōna being 'moon'
craft workers long skipped work after Sunday's drinking, a custom called 'Saint Monday'; Benjamin Franklin boasted of 'never making a St. Monday' as a young London printer in the 1720s

current_meaning: the day of the week after Sunday
